description: #5057 — `undo_page_op`, the positional (depth-addressed) undo. This is the one member of the undo cluster a static fixture can spell today: `undoDepth` is an ORDINAL ("the newest undoable op on this page"), where every other member is given an `OpRef { device_id, seq }` and the two runners' device ids differ. The seed row is edited TWICE because undoing an edit reconstructs the prior text from the op log: a block whose history starts at its seed row has no prior and the undo refuses with `non_reversible`. The return shape names only the two op_type fields for that same reason — `reversed_op_type` is what says WHICH op was undone, and it is the field the frontend turns into its toast (`useUndoShortcuts.ts` builds `undo.op.${snakeToCamel(reversed_op_type)}`).
name: undo_page_op

ops.comment: S2's FIRST op. Undoing an edit reconstructs the prior text from the op log, so a block whose history starts at the seed row has nothing to restore and the undo would refuse with `non_reversible` — this op is what gives the edit below a prior to go back to.
The forward op the undo below reverses.

Depth 0 is the NEWEST undoable op, so this targets the second edit and S2 goes back to `first edit` — the PRIOR text, not the seed content, which is what separates a real reversal from a reset. `reversed_op_type` is `edit_block` (the op undone) and `new_op_type` the reverse op appended in its place.
ops.name: undo_the_newest_op

ops.comment: #2463 — a depth past the end of the page's undoable history is NotFound, not a silent no-op.
ops.name: a_depth_past_the_end_is_not_found

ops.comment: A negative depth is refused before the lookup, so it is Validation where the overrun above is NotFound.
ops.name: a_negative_depth_is_refused

queries.comment: The observation: S2 is back to `first edit` and S3 never moved.
